newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end lower in technical retreat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end lower in technical retreat.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended sharply lower in an acceleration of the technical retracement from four-month highs reached last week, traders said.

After a weak opening, the decline in bond futures gained momentum after the Labor Department said initial jobless claims fell by 14,000 to 332,000 in the week ended June 21. Analysts had looked for a claims figure of 340,000.

Traders said hedge pressure related to recent heavy municipal and corporate bond issuance as well as rumored central bank selling in 10-year Treasurys on Wednesday weighed on Treasury futures and intermediate Eurodollar contracts.

Hedge pressure also stemmed from this week's auction of two- and five-year Treasurys, which may have been well received by the dealer community but ultimately not well distributed in the face of a supply glut, a Eurodollar futures broker said.

A futures trader for a U.S. brokerage house said the September bond contract's previous daily close below 112-02, the low from Friday, confirmed the retracement was under way. The contract on Friday reached a four-month peak at 112-24.
September bonds fell through more critial support levels as prices eroded steadily throughout the session.
The contract in the morning pushed through 111-17, a double bottom from last week, and later broke 110-10, a previously stubborn level whose violation touched off sell-stops, traders said.
News that an American Bankers Association advisory panel was calling for at least a 25 basis point rate hike this summer added fuel to the downturn, some traders said.
The APICS business outlook index, also released this morning, offered only fleeting support to prices, they said. The index fell to 52.4 in June from 53.0 in May.
In addition, a six-point decline in the Conference Board's help wanted advertising index in May, to 81.0, failed to stem the slide, traders said.
Market participants continue to anticipate the Fed will leave interest rates unchanged at its two-day meeting next week, the Eurodollar broker said.
"Most people are completely convinced that nothing is going to happen next Tuesday," he said.
But "they are ever so slightly hedging their bets" on what the Fed might do later in the third quarter, he said.
September bond futures ended 18/32 lower at 111-05, September Treasury note futures were 9/32 lower at 108-02 and December Eurodollars were 0.015 points lower at 93.930.
